reference_title: Eurocode 7: Geotechnical Design - Part 1: General Rules
chapter_title: Fill, dewatering, ground improvement and reinforcement

sections.title: General
sections.summary: Applies where adequate ground conditions are achieved by placing fill (soil/crushed rock/blasted stone/certain waste), dewatering, treating, or reinforcing ground; example placement uses include foundation/slab fills, retaining-structure backfill, general landfill, and small embankments. Dewatering and ground improvement/reinforcement may be temporary or permanent; design procedures for the resulting works follow Sections 6 to 12.
sections.body: The provisions of this Section apply where adequate ground conditions are achieved by placing natural soil, crushed rock, blasted stone or certain waste products; by dewatering; by treating ground; or by reinforcing ground. Situations where soil or granular material is placed for engineering purposes include fills beneath foundations and ground slabs, backfill to excavations and retaining structures, general landfill (including hydraulic fill, landscape mounds and spoil heaps), and embankments for small dams and infrastructure. Dewatering of ground may be temporary or permanent, and ground treated to improve its properties (natural ground or fill) may likewise be temporary or permanent. Design procedures for geotechnical works using fill, dewatering, improvement, or reinforcement shall be those presented in Sections 6 to 12.
key_points: Covers ground conditions achieved via fill placement, dewatering, ground treatment, or ground reinforcement
Typical fill uses: foundation/slab support, retaining-structure backfill, landfill, small embankments
Dewatering and ground improvement/reinforcement may be temporary or permanent
The resulting geotechnical works are designed per Sections 6-12
sections.applicability: Scope-setting clause for fill, dewatering, and ground improvement/reinforcement works.

sections.title: Fundamental requirements
sections.summary: Fill and dewatered/improved/reinforced ground must sustain the actions from its function and environment, and this requirement extends to the ground on which the fill is placed.
sections.body: Fill and dewatered, improved or reinforced ground shall be capable of sustaining the actions arising from its function and from its environment. These fundamental requirements shall also be satisfied for the ground on which the fill is placed.
key_points: Fill/treated ground must sustain functional and environmental actions
The underlying ground on which fill is placed must also meet these requirements
sections.applicability: Baseline performance requirement for all fill/dewatering/improvement/reinforcement works.

sections.title: Fill construction - Principles
sections.summary: Fill design must consider good material handling properties and adequate post-compaction engineering properties, with transport and placement also considered in design.
sections.body: When designing fill constructions it shall be considered that the adequacy of the fill depends on good material handling properties and adequate engineering properties after compaction. Transport and placement of the fill should be considered in the design.
key_points: Fill adequacy depends on handling properties and post-compaction engineering properties
Transport and placement methods are design considerations
sections.applicability: Governing principles for fill design ahead of material selection and placement procedure.

sections.title: Fill construction - Selection of fill material
sections.summary: Fill material selection criteria target adequate post-compaction strength/stiffness/durability/permeability for the fill's purpose; suitable materials include graded granular soils and select waste products; specification must weigh grading, crushing resistance, compactibility, permeability, plasticity, organic content, chemical aggression, solubility, volume-change susceptibility, frost susceptibility, and cementation potential, with unsuitable materials adjusted, mixed, processed, protected, or drained, and frozen/expansive/soluble soils normally excluded.
sections.body: Criteria for specifying suitable fill material shall be based on achieving adequate strength, stiffness, durability, and permeability after compaction, taking account of the fill's purpose and any supported structure's requirements. Suitable fill materials may include most graded natural granular materials and certain waste products (e.g. selected colliery waste, pulverised fuel ash); some manufactured materials (e.g. light aggregate) and some cohesive materials may also be used, the latter with particular care. Specification must account for grading, crushing resistance, compactibility, permeability, plasticity, strength of underlying ground, organic content, chemical aggression, pollution effects, solubility, susceptibility to volume changes (swelling clays, collapsible materials), low temperature/frost susceptibility, weathering resistance, effects of excavation/transport/placement, and cementation potential (e.g. blast furnace slags). If local materials in their natural state are unsuitable, procedures such as adjusting water content, mixing with cement/lime/other materials, crushing/sieving/washing, protecting with appropriate material, or using drainage layers may be adopted. Frozen, expansive, or soluble soils should not normally be used as fill. Where selected material contains potentially aggressive/polluting chemicals, adequate provisions shall prevent attack on structures/services or ground-water pollution, and such materials shall only be used in large amounts at permanently monitored locations. Where in doubt, fill material shall be tested at source, with test type/number/frequency selected per material type/heterogeneity and project nature (inspection may suffice for Geotechnical Category 1). Material for fill with severe bearing resistance/settlement/stability requirements shall not contain significant snow, ice, or peat; fills with no such specified requirements may contain small amounts.
key_points: Selection criteria target post-compaction strength, stiffness, durability, and permeability
Suitable fills: graded granular natural materials, select waste products, some manufactured/cohesive materials
Long checklist of specification factors: grading, plasticity, chemical aggression, frost susceptibility, cementation potential, etc.
Unsuitable natural materials may be adjusted (water content, admixtures, processing, protection, drainage)
Frozen/expansive/soluble soils normally excluded; aggressive/polluting materials need special provisions and monitoring
Testing at source is required in cases of doubt, scaled by material type and project nature
sections.applicability: Material selection and specification requirements for engineered fill.

sections.title: Fill construction - Selection of procedures for fill placement and compaction
sections.summary: Compaction criteria are set per fill zone/layer per its purpose; placement/compaction procedures must ensure stability throughout construction without adversely affecting the natural subsoil, driven by material origin/nature, placement method/water content, lift thickness, climate, compaction uniformity, and underlying ground; a trial compaction establishes the procedure and control criteria, with rainfall run-off profiling and freezing-temperature protection considered, backfill compacted to avoid damaging subsidence, fill placed on undisturbed drained ground (with a filter to prevent mixing), and soft underwater material removed before placement.
sections.body: Compaction criteria shall be established for each zone or layer of fill, related to its purpose and performance requirements. Placement/compaction procedures shall be specified so that fill stability is ensured throughout construction without adversely affecting the natural subsoil, depending on compaction criteria and on the origin/nature of the material, the placement method, placement water content and its variation, initial/final lift thickness, local climatic conditions, compaction uniformity, and the nature of the underlying ground. A trial compaction at the site, using the intended material and equipment, should be performed to determine the compaction procedure (placement method, equipment, layer thickness, number of passes, transportation technique, water addition) and may also establish control criteria. Where rainfall is possible during placement of cohesive fill, the surface should be profiled at all stages to permit run-off; at sub-freezing temperatures, fill may need heating before placement and frost protection of the surface, assessed case-by-case. Backfill placed around foundations and beneath floor slabs shall be compacted so damaging subsidence does not occur. Fill should be placed on an undisturbed, drained ground surface, with mixing of fill and ground prevented by a filter textile or layer; before placing fill underwater, all soft material encountered should be removed by dredging or other means.
key_points: Compaction criteria set per fill zone/layer according to its purpose
Placement/compaction procedure depends on material, method, water content, lift thickness, climate, and underlying ground
A field trial compaction determines the procedure and may set control criteria
Rainfall run-off profiling and frost protection are procedural considerations
Backfill compaction must avoid damaging subsidence; fill placed on undisturbed, drained, filtered ground
sections.applicability: Construction procedure requirements for placing and compacting fill.

sections.title: Fill construction - Checking the fill
sections.summary: Fill is inspected/tested for material, placement water content, and compaction procedure compliance (testing may be waived where procedures are proven by trial/experience); compaction is checked via dry density/water content measurement, penetration/stiffness measurement (not reliable alone for cohesive soils), or (for rock fill) field methods since the Proctor test does not apply; over-compaction limits are specified where relevant, since over-compaction can cause slickensides/high stiffness in slopes, high earth pressures on retaining structures, and crushing of soft materials.
sections.body: Fill shall be inspected or tested to ensure material, placement water content, and compaction procedures comply with the specification; testing need not be performed for material/procedure combinations already proved by field trial or comparable experience. Compaction should be tested by measuring dry density (and water content if required), or by measuring properties such as penetration resistance or stiffness (which cannot always confirm satisfactory compaction in cohesive soils). Minimum fill densities (e.g. by Proctor percentage) should be specified and checked on site; for rock fill or fill with a large amount of coarse particles, compaction should be checked by field methods since the Proctor test is not applicable. Site checking (EN 1997-2) may use compliance with a field-trial/experience-derived procedure, checking additional-pass settlement against a specified value, plate loading tests, or seismic/dynamic methods. Where over-compaction is unacceptable, an upper bound compaction limit shall be specified; over-compaction can cause slickensides and high stiffness in slopes, high earth pressures on buried/retaining structures, and crushing of materials such as soft rocks, slags, and volcanic sands used as lightweight fills.
key_points: Fill checking covers material, placement water content, and compaction procedure compliance
Compaction testing methods: dry density/water content, penetration/stiffness, or (rock fill) field methods
Proctor test does not apply to rock fill or fill with much coarse material
Over-compaction limits may be required; over-compaction risks include high earth pressures and material crushing
sections.applicability: Quality control and acceptance criteria for placed and compacted fill.

sections.title: Dewatering
sections.summary: Dewatering schemes must be based on geotechnical/hydrogeological investigation and may use gravity drainage, sump/wellpoint/bored-well pumping, or electro-osmosis (possibly with recharge wells); design must ensure excavation stability, avoid excessive settlement/ground loss/damage, provide adequate filtering, and maintain designed water levels; effectiveness is checked by monitoring water levels/pressures/movements, with long-duration pumping also checked for corrosion/clogging risk.
sections.body: Any scheme for removing water from the ground or lowering water pressure shall be based on the results of a geotechnical or hydrogeological investigation. Water may be removed by gravity drainage, pumping from sumps/well points/bored wells, or electro-osmosis, with the scheme depending on existing ground/ground-water conditions and project characteristics (excavation depth, dewatering extent); part of the scheme may include recharge wells at a distance from the excavation. The dewatering scheme should ensure, as appropriate: excavation sides remain stable under ground-water lowering, without excessive heave or base rupture (e.g. from excessive water pressure beneath a less permeable layer); no excessive settlement or damage to nearby structures; no excessive loss of ground by seepage; adequate filters around sumps (except for fairly uniformly graded self-filtering material) to prevent soil transport with pumped water; removed water discharged far enough from the excavated area; designed water levels/pore pressures maintained without significant fluctuation; adequate pumping capacity with back-up for breakdowns; care against collapse of sensitive soils (e.g. loose sand) when ground-water returns to its original level; and avoidance of excessive contaminated-water transport or extraction in a drinking-water catchment. Dewatering effectiveness shall be checked by monitoring ground-water level, pore pressures, and ground movements as necessary, with frequent data review to determine effects on ground conditions and nearby structures. Long-duration pumping shall be checked for dissolved salts/gases (risk of well screen corrosion or clogging from salt precipitation), and long-term dewatering systems shall be designed to prevent clogging by bacterial action or other causes.
key_points: Dewatering schemes must be based on geotechnical/hydrogeological investigation
Methods: gravity drainage, sump/wellpoint/bored-well pumping, electro-osmosis, with optional recharge wells
Design considerations: excavation stability, settlement control, filtering, water-level control, pumping capacity/back-up
Effectiveness monitored via water level, pore pressure, and ground movement; long-duration pumping checked for corrosion/clogging risk
sections.applicability: Design and monitoring requirements for temporary or permanent ground dewatering schemes.

sections.title: Ground improvement and reinforcement
sections.summary: Ground improvement/reinforcement method selection requires a prior geotechnical investigation and consideration of ground/fill thickness/properties, water pressure, structure nature/size/position, prevention of damage to adjacent structures, temporary-vs-permanent duration, deformation-construction sequence interaction, environmental effects (pollution, ground-water level changes), and long-term material deterioration; effectiveness is checked against acceptance criteria via induced changes in the relevant ground properties.
sections.body: A geotechnical investigation of the initial ground conditions shall be carried out before any ground improvement or reinforcement method is chosen or used. The ground improvement method shall be designed taking into account, where appropriate: thickness and properties of the ground or fill material; magnitude of water pressure in the various strata; nature, size, and position of the supported structure; prevention of damage to adjacent structures or services; whether the improvement is temporary or permanent; the relationship between the improvement method and the construction sequence in terms of anticipated deformations; environmental effects including pollution by toxic substances or ground-water level changes; and long-term material deterioration. The effectiveness of the ground improvement shall be checked against acceptance criteria by determining the induced changes in the appropriate ground properties.
key_points: Requires a geotechnical investigation before selecting an improvement/reinforcement method
Design factors: ground/fill properties, water pressure, structure characteristics, adjacent-structure protection, duration, environmental effects
Effectiveness checked via measured induced changes in relevant ground properties against acceptance criteria
sections.applicability: Design and verification framework for ground improvement and reinforcement methods.
